stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia's hold on China's AI-chip market slipped: Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months, taking sales Nvidia once had there. The same week, a leaked White House ballroom donor list showed Nvidia gave $25 million to an administration that decides its export licences.

stocks:ASML.standing: The Dutch company that builds the lithography machines chipmakers use to print circuits, and the only supplier of the extreme-ultraviolet tools that leading-edge chips need. Export rules decide who may buy them.
stocks:ASML.recent: China's share of ASML's sales jumped from 14% to 23%, with its equipment sales there up 109% despite a US push to curb exports. Earlier, BofA said an ASML chip technology move threatened Besi's shares. Neither accounts for the line: the China figures came out after the last close shown.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu heads the government formed after Israel's next election. The premiership needs a 61-seat Knesset majority, so coalition arithmetic moves it as much as votes do.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Israel marked three years since October 7 ahead of elections, and the anniversary reopened the question of who carries the blame: former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar is suing Netanyahu for 3 million shekels in defamation over it. Nothing in the fortnight's reporting accounts for what traders will pay.

stocks:T.standing: One of the three national US mobile networks, alongside Verizon and T-Mobile, and a large fibre broadband provider. A heavy debt load and a long-paid dividend make it a stock held mainly for income.
stocks:T.recent: SpaceX struck a nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile, putting a satellite rival onto the kind of airwaves AT&T and Verizon sell service on, and both shares dropped 7% that day. Days later AT&T agreed to sell its Mexican business, 24.7 million subscribers, for $2 billion, ending its push into Mexico.

stocks:TLEVISACPO.MX.standing: Mexico's largest broadcaster, listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange, which also runs the izzi cable and broadband network and Sky satellite TV. Its share tracks Mexican household spending on pay TV and connectivity.
stocks:TLEVISACPO.MX.recent: Televisa agreed to pay $2 billion for AT&T's Mexican business and its 24.7 million subscribers, which turns a cable and broadband company into a mobile operator as well. The deal came at the end of the window, and nothing in the input explains the earlier swings in the share.

stocks:TEL.OL.standing: Norway's largest telecoms operator, majority-owned by the Norwegian state, running mobile networks across the Nordics and in Asia. Its dividend makes it a staple of Norwegian pension and income portfolios.
stocks:TEL.OL.recent: Plaintiffs in Oslo sued Telenor, saying it gave Myanmar's junta 1,253 phone numbers and then sold the network, with its call records and location data, to a junta-linked buyer. The suit was filed after the last close on the chart, so it does not explain the slide before it.

wiki-china.standing: The daily count of readers of Wikipedia's article on China, the world's second-largest economy and its largest exporter. It shows how often the country's affairs send a general audience to look it up.
wiki-china.recent: China's news over the fortnight was mostly trade and technology. The EU planned measures to cut imports of Chinese hybrid cars by half, Beijing drafted an export-control list covering 23 AI technologies including model weights, and the central bank bought 23 tonnes of gold in September. None of it falls on the day the series peaked.

wiki-data-center.standing: A building packed with the servers, storage and network gear that run websites, cloud services and AI models. Its hunger for electricity and cooling now shapes grid planning and power deals.
wiki-data-center.recent: Ukrainian drones made Russia's data centres a front line: a second Yandex site in Kaluga was partly disabled, later strikes hit 3 of Yandex's 6 Russian data centers, and a drone struck Sberbank's data centre in Balakovo. Kyiv's campaign took aim at Russia's AI data infrastructure rather than its oil depots alone.

stocks:FFH.TO.standing: A Toronto holding company that owns property and casualty insurers and reinsurers around the world and invests their premiums, run by Prem Watsa in a value style. It has built large stakes in Indian companies.
stocks:FFH.TO.recent: Fairfax won 60.72% of IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore, India's largest privatisation, which puts the insurer's balance sheet in control of an Indian lender. The award came after the chart's last close, so none of the line reflects it, and nothing in the input explains the earlier moves.

stocks:PLTR.standing: Palantir Technologies, a US software company listed on Nasdaq, sells data-analysis platforms to defence ministries, intelligence agencies and large corporations. Government contracts make up a large share of its revenue.
stocks:PLTR.recent: France chose Chapsvision over another Palantir contract as European governments questioned their dependence on the company, and Louis Mosley warned that Europe was 'missing the boat' on AI. Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the share price itself.

stocks:GFS.standing: A contract chipmaker that builds other companies' designs, specialising in older, cheaper process nodes used in cars, phones, radios and defence electronics. It is one of the few foundries headquartered in the US.
stocks:GFS.recent: Washington doubled its equity stake in GlobalFoundries to nearly 8% and will partner with it on a new fab at Malta, New York, a step from CHIPS Act grants to outright ownership. The deal came after this chart's last close, so it does not account for the rise shown here.

stocks:RELIANCE.NS.standing: India's most valuable listed company, a Mumbai conglomerate that runs the Jamnagar refining complex alongside Jio telecoms and India's biggest retail chain. Its size makes it a swing stock for the whole Indian market.
stocks:RELIANCE.NS.recent: Reliance is floating Jio Platforms, its telecom arm, in what it priced as India's largest offering, seeking up to ₹30,213 crore; the $3.2 billion sale drew nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore of demand, sovereign funds among the bidders. Separately, Reliance answered Musk over Starlink, saying its own satellite service awaits the same clearances.

stocks:ACN.standing: One of the world's largest consulting and IT-services firms, incorporated in Ireland and listed in New York. Its shares track how much corporations spend on outsourcing, and lately on help adopting AI.
stocks:ACN.recent: The one story about Accenture's own business was a cost cut: staff who had spent up to $1,000 a month on Claude were capped at $29, a firm that sells AI transformation to clients now rationing it for its own workers. It landed at the end of the rise, which began in late September, and does not account for it.

stocks:NESN.SW.standing: The world's largest packaged-food company, based in Vevey, Switzerland, selling Nescafé, Maggi, Purina and infant formula almost everywhere. A heavyweight of the Swiss SMI, its share moves with coffee, cocoa and dairy costs.
stocks:NESN.SW.recent: India's food regulator, FSSAI, found a Nestlé dairy whitener sample unsafe and substandard, in a wider crackdown that also suspended a confectionery firm and recalled cumin; Nestle said the product was safe. The share's trough came the next day. Nothing reported since accounts for the recovery.

stocks:BA.L.standing: Britain's largest defence company, building warships, nuclear submarines, combat aircraft and munitions, with a large US arm. Its shares move on NATO governments' defence budgets and the export orders they approve.
stocks:BA.L.recent: A cyberattack on BAE Systems, working as a contractor for the US courts, halted all notices for US bankruptcy courts. The attack was reported in Washington after the slide had already happened, and nothing else in the input explains the price.

stocks:TSLA.standing: Shares in Tesla, the US maker of electric cars and grid batteries, listed on Nasdaq. Its valuation rests more on bets about self-driving cars and robots than on the cars it sells today, so it moves on Elon Musk's promises.
stocks:TSLA.recent: The fortnight's news about Tesla's own business was Musk's push into India stalling alongside Starlink, and the debut of a 2026 Roadster priced at at least $200,000, which came after the latest reading on the chart. Neither accounts for the share's path across the window.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Apple's shares, traded on the Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from the iPhone, and its weight as one of the world's most valuable companies means its moves carry the S&P 500 and Nasdaq indices with it.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Pre-orders for the iPhone Duo opened and the phone was backordered until 2027 on the first day. In the same week Apple Intelligence entered China running on Alibaba's Qwen models, the route Apple took to approval there. Days earlier Apple introduced HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The first cryptocurrency, a fixed-supply digital currency run on a public ledger with no central issuer, launched in 2009. Its price sets the tone for the whole crypto market, and funds, banks and listed companies now hold it.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Nothing reported explains the spike early in the window. The weeks after were about bitcoin and quantum computing: Google's Willow chip cut magic-state errors about 40-fold, and 6.4 million bitcoin sit behind public keys already exposed. MSCI's rules, meanwhile, put the bitcoin treasury firms Strategy and Metaplanet on notice.

stocks:MSTR.standing: A Nasdaq-listed software company that became the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, funding its purchases by selling new shares and debt. Its stock trades as a leveraged bet on the bitcoin price.
stocks:MSTR.recent: MSCI finalised rules that can eject companies whose main business is holding bitcoin from its equity indexes, putting Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet on notice. JPMorgan estimates $2.8 billion of forced selling of Strategy shares. The funds sell the stock, not the bitcoin, which squeezes the cheap equity the firm raises to buy more.

stocks:JPM.standing: America's largest bank by assets, spanning Chase consumer branches, a leading investment bank and a vast trading operation. Its quarterly results open US bank earnings season and are read as a check on the economy's health.
stocks:JPM.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley in a review of bank lending to private credit, prompted by worries over that market. When results arrived, a $1.2B money laundering penalty drove Bank of America to an earnings miss while JPMorgan Chase held steady.

stocks:3350.T.standing: A Tokyo-listed company that turned from running budget hotels to holding bitcoin as its main asset, and sells new shares to buy more. Its stock works as a leveraged bet on bitcoin for investors in Japan.
stocks:3350.T.recent: MSCI finalised rules that can eject companies whose main business is holding bitcoin from its equity indexes, Metaplanet among them. Index funds then sell the shares, not the bitcoin, which cuts at the cheap equity the firm raises to buy more; JPMorgan put the forced selling of Strategy alone at $2.8 billion.

stocks:MSCI.standing: The New York company whose stock indexes, among them MSCI World and MSCI Emerging Markets, decide what trillions of dollars in tracking funds must own. It also sells ESG ratings and risk analytics, and its fees grow with the assets benchmarked to it.
stocks:MSCI.recent: MSCI finalised rules that can eject bitcoin-holding firms such as Strategy and Metaplanet from its indexes, with JPMorgan estimating $2.8 billion of forced selling of Strategy alone. It also moved to strip Indonesia of emerging-market status, sending Jakarta to a six-year low. Nothing reported ties either decision to MSCI's own share price.

stocks:HSBA.L.standing: One of Europe's largest banks, headquartered in London but earning most of its profit in Asia, above all in Hong Kong. Its London shares move on Asian interest rates and on the state of relations between China and the West.

stocks:TSM.standing: Shares of the world's largest contract chipmaker, which fabricates the most advanced processors for Apple, Nvidia and others from plants in Taiwan. Its order book is a direct read on demand for AI and smartphone chips.

stocks:INTC.standing: An American chipmaker that both designs and manufactures its own processors, which run most PCs and many servers. Its foundry arm, making chips for other firms, carries Washington's push for US-made semiconductors.

stocks:JD.standing: One of China's largest online retailers, listed in New York and Hong Kong. Unlike its rivals it owns its warehouses and delivery fleet, so its sales track what Chinese households are spending.
stocks:JD.recent: The fortnight carried one story about the company's own business: it ended deposit pre-sales for its 18th Singles' Day. That story ran after the shares had already peaked, and nothing in it accounts for the price.

wiki-international-monetary-fund.standing: The Washington-based lender to governments in balance-of-payments crises, owned by nearly every country. Its loans come with budget conditions, and its twice-yearly growth forecasts set the baseline finance ministries argue against.
wiki-international-monetary-fund.recent: At its meetings with the World Bank in Bangkok, the IMF lifted its world growth forecast to 3.1% but saw Kuwait shrinking 16.7% as the Hormuz closure dragged on. Its chief called for urgent repairs to public finances: low-income countries spend 14% of revenue on debt, and developing countries face $400 billion in external payments this year.

wiki-india.standing: Wikipedia's article on India, the world's most populous country and its largest democracy. How many people open it each day is a rough measure of how often the wider world stops to look the country up.
wiki-india.recent: Delhi Police turned the detention of Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, into an arrest after a week of protests in New Delhi demanding that election chief Gyanesh Kumar resign over voter-roll revisions that removed 133 million names since last year. One flag march met 6,000 police.

poly-no-hormuz-agreement-by-nov-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no agreement is reached over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf's only sea exit. About a fifth of the world's oil normally passes through it.
poly-no-hormuz-agreement-by-nov-2.recent: Bets against a deal climbed as the strait turned more violent: six ships were hit in one day, two Emirati cargo ships sank, and the IRGC said a supertanker struck a mine on a 'prohibited' route, while Iran's army tied reopening to its rights. Iran's 7-day reopening plan, reported by state-run Press TV, came after the peak.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if David Lisnard, the centre-right mayor of Cannes, wins France's 2027 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

stocks:V.standing: The largest card payment network in the world, routing transactions between the banks that issue cards and those that accept them. It earns a fee on each payment and lends nothing, so its revenue tracks consumer spending.

stocks:CRCL.standing: The US company that issues USDC, a dollar stablecoin backed by cash and short-dated Treasuries. Most of its revenue is interest on those reserves, so the share tracks US short-term rates and how much USDC circulates.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-ilhan-omar-federally-charged-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if federal prosecutors charge Ilhan Omar, the Democratic congresswoman from Minnesota, before its deadline. The price is what traders pay for that payout.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's government and allied forces enter Sanaa, the capital the Houthis have held since 2014, by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay on the city changing hands.
poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.recent: The government's claimed gains came on the Red Sea coast, not on the road to Sanaa: it said it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road on its push toward Bab al-Mandeb. The Houthis meanwhile struck Riyadh's airport again, killing at least 3. The government's claim of 800 Houthi casualties in a day came through TASS.

stocks:LYFT.standing: Shares in Lyft, the second-largest ride-hailing app in the United States after Uber, sold almost entirely on the US and Canadian market. Its price turns on rider demand, driver pay and rules for gig workers.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-us-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris, the former vice-president and 2024 Democratic nominee, wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

stocks:UBER.standing: Shares in Uber, the largest ride-hailing and food-delivery platform outside China, listed in New York. The price tracks how many trips and orders it brokers and how much of each fare it keeps.
stocks:UBER.recent: The one story about Uber's own business came after the last close shown. Consumer Reports looked into how its AI pricing sets fares and found that same-minute quotes for one trip differed by 42.4%. Nothing earlier in the input accounts for the share price.

poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran and Oman, the two states whose coasts form the Strait of Hormuz, reach an agreement on the strait before its deadline. About a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through that channel.
poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.recent: Bets on a deal faded as attacks on shipping mounted: 12 ships were attacked near Hormuz in one week, two sank, and Iran's army said the strait stays closed until its rights are respected. Araghchi's reopening proposal, carried by Press TV, blamed the US-Israeli war, while US planners drafted strikes with a 21,600-pound bomb.

wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the former actor and comedian elected Ukraine's president in 2019, who has led the country through Russia's full-scale invasion.
wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.recent: Trump said Ukraine should elect a new president, claiming Zelenskyy has lost 30% of Ukraine. Kyiv then offered to stop refinery strikes if Russia stopped hitting energy sites, and Russia struck a Kharkiv power plant after Trump's truce. Days later Ukraine ran out of Patriot interceptors, and almost every ballistic missile in the next strike got through.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire by the end of October. Its price is what traders will stake on a truce, and Gulf oil exports and Red Sea shipping ride on it.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: Traders backed away from a deal as the war moved onto Saudi soil: a Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport killed 13, a missile set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran, and the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell. Egypt has since approved troops for Saudi Arabia, and Saudi National Guard officers died in a helicopter crash near Najran.
